That is too late - it is checked when iplots is loaded which is when JGR is loaded. In addition, the value doesn't matter it should be empty (Sys.setenv(NOAWT="")) or unset. Any value (even 0) enables it.

That is more than odd .. please check your R startup files (.Renviron, .Rprofile). NOAWT should really never be set - it is used only internally by our checking system to bootstrap JGR builds (because the JGR package needs to be built by R before JGR can be run yet it only works in JGR). To be honest I can't think of any way that it could be set inadvertently... 

Cheers,
Simon

JRI and Rserve are entirely different ways to call R from Java. If you already use JRI then calling Rserve doesn't make much sense - the point of Rserve is that you avoid embedding the R process into your application (which is what JRI does).
